LESSON: BEEF FARMING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES IN EASTERN AFRICA Strand Sub- Strand Specific 
Topic 3.1: Beef Farming

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Beef Farming. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How could we benefit from large-scale farming?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa
2. identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa
3. explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BEEF FARMING
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Beef Farming helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: BEEF FARMING
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Beef Farming” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Beef Farming.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Beef Farming is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Beef Farming” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Beef Farming. (skill: identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Beef Farming to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa.
3. Practise this skill: identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa.
4. Practise this skill: explain the challenges facing beef farming and possible solutions in Eastern Africa.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Beef Farming from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Beef Farming: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Beef Farming?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How could we benefit from large-scale farming?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Beef Farming means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa.
5. Be able to: identify the contribution of beef farming to the economy of Eastern Africa.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
